newsitem.title: NORWAY: FINNISH POWER GRID WANTS TO BUY ELEX.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH POWER GRID WANTS TO BUY ELEX.

text.p: Finnish Power Grid Ltd wants to buy Finland's electricity exchange Elex, Juha Kekkonen, the grid company's CEO, told Reuters.
Elex is currently run by Finnish derivatives exchange SOM, which is due to merge with the Helsinki Stock Exchange.
"There are negotiations going on," Kekkonen said, but he would not specify a timeframe for an outcome.
"We are evaluating different options in the effort to integrate the grid into the Nordic market. Buying Elex is one of them," he said.
The possible purchase is part a strategy to integrate Finland into the merged Norwegian-Swedish electricity market, according to Kekkonen.
"What we're trying to do is to establish a real Nordic power market, which means, of course, that Finland needs to be included," Kekkonen said.

The Finnish power-transmission network company was formally established in November last year, but will not start operations until September 1, as it takes on responsibility for the country's foreign electricity-exchange systems in addition to the domestic grid.
"The system will be up and going about two weeks from now," Kekkonen said.
"The goal is to facilitate free transmission exchange across borders," he added. "It is still premature, but we definitely want it to happen."
The grid company's majority share holder is state-owned power company Imatran Voima Oy (IVO), which holds 25 percent of the shares and 33 percent of the voting rights.
The Finnish state, Pohjolan Voima Oy (PVO) and a number of private institutional investors own the remaining stake.
Finnish Power Grid paid IVO 5,35 billion Finnish markkaa for the right to operate Finland's grid system, according to IVO.
If the grid company succeeds in taking over Elex, it would strengthen its position on the Nordic power market, according to Kekkonen.
